Statement: Benchmark biomedical ECG and multimodal CVD datasets (PTB-XL, MIMIC-IV, Chapman-Shaoxing, ARIC, UK Biobank) severely under-represent or exclude South Asian and Bangladeshi cohorts.
Contradictions: P0030 cites Singapore SEED Indian subgroup (AUC 0.94, p. 13) alongside severe provenance/editorial contradictions; P0005 includes 3,091 broad Asian patients without South Asian granularity.
Uncertainty: True cross-site generalization to Bangladeshi clinical populations remains empirically untested.

Statement: Even in a Bangladeshi-led systematic review and meta-analysis of 85 DL-ECG studies, zero primary studies used Bangladeshi cohorts and 0/85 (0%) quantified prediction uncertainty.
Contradictions: P0022 includes 400 rows sampled from CAIR-CVD-2025 (Bangladesh) without disclosing Bangladeshi hospital provenance or raw ECG waveforms.
Uncertainty: Country breakdown in P0041 covers 85 studies in Fig. 1e while Table 1 enumerates 84 rows.

Statement: The only included primary study referencing the Bangladeshi CAIR-CVD-2025 dataset combines only tabular/wearable features without 12-lead ECG waveforms and exhibits High PROBAST Risk of Bias due to pre-split SMOTE, KNN imputation, Z-score normalization, and EQI-BGWO feature selection.
Contradictions: P0022 §5.2 (p. 12) claims post-split separation despite Methods text/diagrams explicitly placing balancing and normalization before splitting.
Uncertainty: CAIR-CVD-2025 total N=1,529 is downsampled to 400 rows in Fig. 1 without explanation.

Statement: In a formal PROBAST audit of 108 AI-ECG studies, only 11.1% (12/108) achieved Low Risk of Bias while 34.3% (37/108) were High Risk and 54.6% (59/108) were Moderate or Unclear Risk, driven primarily by Participant selection (31.5% High) and Analysis flaws (33.3% High).
SourceLocators: P0042 (p. 9 Table 3, pp. 4-5 Fig. 1, p. 8 Table 2)
Contradictions: P0010 similarly found 34.5% (16/46) High Risk of Bias among EHR ML CVD models via PROBAST (p. 10).
Uncertainty: P0042 searched PubMed and Cochrane only and noted 108-study country details reside in unbundled supplements.

Statement: Full-text PROBAST auditing of all 29 original empirical studies in our curated 42-paper portfolio identified High Risk of Bias in 25/29 (86.2%), Unclear in 3/29 (10.3%), and Low Risk in only 1/29 (3.4%, P0038), with recurring patient-overlap/segment splitting and pre-split preprocessing leakage.
Contradictions: P0005, P0023, and P0025 demonstrate patient-level splitting without leakage but rate Unclear due to omitted calibration/DCA or missing supplementary counts.
Uncertainty: Risk ratings reflect dual-extracted PDF text without access to unbundled online-only supplements.

Statement: Most multimodal CVD prediction models fuse only two data types (e.g., ECG+Labs, ECG+EHR, ECG+PCG, or ECG+CXR), and systematic synthesis in HF (P0017) confirms 0/15 included studies combined >=3 modalities or paired clinical/ECG with lifestyle inputs.
Contradictions: P0016, P0025, P0031, P0036, and P0038 integrate 3-4 modalities, typically incorporating Cardiac MRI/CT/Echo, proteomics, or clinical text rather than accessible 4-modality screening (Clinical+ECG+Lab+Lifestyle).
Uncertainty: Exclusion of cardiac imaging in our FYDP differentiates accessible primary screening fusion from tertiary CMR/CCTA models.

Statement: Lifestyle predictors (smoking, physical activity, diet) are rarely integrated as an explicit fusion modality alongside 12-lead ECG and serum biomarkers, and none of the reviewed multimodal ECG+tabular studies quantified lifestyle incremental gain via controlled Leave-One-Modality-Out (LOMO) ablation.
Contradictions: P0020, P0021, P0025, and P0036 include smoking history as a tabular EHR indicator, and P0022 models lifestyle without raw ECG waveforms.
Uncertainty: Incremental predictive benefit of lifestyle variables may be modest relative to ECG and serum biomarkers and must be empirically tested in RQ2.

Statement: Across 65 healthcare XAI studies reviewed in P0034, 61.5% (40/65) included no explainability, zero attention-based studies tested attribution faithfulness, and only 2/25 XAI studies conducted clinician plausibility evaluation.
Contradictions: P0035 qualitatively reviewed 45 ECG-XAI studies and corroborated that evaluation remains fragmented without consensus faithfulness benchmarks.
Uncertainty: Review-level counts depend on P0034's screening consistency (which mixed non-XAI papers despite exclusion wording).

Statement: Full-text verification disproved 20 of 24 preliminary quantitative-XAI flags in papers.csv: zero multimodal ECG+Clinical+Lab+Lifestyle models evaluated multimodal SHAP deletion/insertion AOPC faithfulness, multi-seed attribution stability, and cardiologist plausibility jointly.
Contradictions: P0038 achieved Low PROBAST risk with blinded 3-cardiologist rationale review (ICC=0.91) and rationale-shuffling ablations, but modeled CMR+EHR+Text without ECG or SHAP AOPC; P0029 deletion AOPC (1.803) failed to outperform random masking (1.846).
Uncertainty: Absence in our 42-paper curated corpus does not replace update searches prior to final modeling/submission.

Statement: Recent multimodal Transformer and gated-fusion frameworks generally outperform unimodal ECG or EHR baselines on matched benchmarks, though performance degrades substantially under temporal drift or external hospital validation.
Contradictions: In P0003 6-month post-PCI mortality (EMR AUC 0.913 > Fusion 0.897) and P0021 external MIMIC pericarditis (ECG 0.818 > Fusion 0.810), fusion failed to beat the best unimodal branch.
Uncertainty: Cross-paper AUCs cannot be ranked directly due to heterogeneous endpoints, sample sizes, and split integrity.

Statement: Probability calibration and Decision Curve Analysis (DCA) are frequently omitted or misapplied in multimodal CVD deep learning studies, whereas SMOTE oversampling directly induces risk overestimation.
SourceLocators: P0019 (p. 63); P0027 (Table 34 p. 28: 45% calibration); P0031 (p. 6 Suppl. Fig. 8); P0038 (Table 2 p. 7, Fig. 5 p. 8)
Contradictions: P0007, P0013, P0021, P0025, and P0038 report Brier, IBS, HL, or DCA metrics.
Uncertainty: Requires strict post-hoc validation-only calibration (Platt/temperature/isotonic) and DCA evaluation in S12-S13.

Statement: Enforcing strict architectural transparency (e.g., Linear or VAE-SCAN models) over black-box ECG ResNets incurs steep predictive performance penalties (-11.22% and additional -5.33% drops), motivating faithful post-hoc explainability for deep fusion architectures.
Contradictions: Evaluated on unimodal ECG regression/mortality (BIDMC/CODE) rather than multimodal tabular+ECG cross-attention fusion.
Uncertainty: Magnitude of trade-off on smaller primary cohorts with rich tabular EHR remains to be measured empirically.
